svg.title: Three query languages, one query engine
svg.desc: Three boxes at the top feed one Dataverse query engine. OData query options are URL text used by the Web API, Xrm.WebApi, code apps, the Python SDK and the Dataverse connector. FetchXML is an XML document used by views, charts, Power Pages, flows, the Web API fetchXml parameter and the SDK FetchExpression; it has the widest feature set: aggregates, joins without a relationship, column comparison and distinct. QueryExpression is a .NET object model used by plug-ins and .NET clients through IOrganizationService.RetrieveMultiple; it is typed and composable but has no default sort order. All three pass through the same engine, which applies the caller's security roles and returns at most 5,000 rows per page for standard tables. Two conversion messages connect FetchXML and QueryExpression: FetchXmlToQueryExpression and QueryExpressionToFetchXml. A bottom strip gives the decision: stay with the language of your client; switch to FetchXML when you need what only it can express.
svg.text: Three ways to write a query; one engine answers them
No default sort order: add one
Applies the caller's security roles and column security.
At most 5,000 rows per page (500 for elastic tables).
Stay with the language your client speaks. Reach for FetchXML when you need an aggregate, a join without a
relationship, a column-to-column comparison, distinct rows, or a query that a view or flow must also use.
